description: A clinic employs nurses and pharmacists to deliver shots to patients. A nurse works 5 hours per shift while a pharmacist works 7 hours per shift. Nurses are paid $250 per shift while pharmacists are paid $300 per shift. Currently, the clinic needs 200 hours of healthcare labor to meet needs. If the firm has a budget of $9000, how many of each healthcare worker should be scheduled to minimize the total number of workers?

NurseShiftHours.definition: Number of hours a nurse works per shift

PharmacistShiftHours.definition: Number of hours a pharmacist works per shift

NurseCostPerShift.definition: Cost to employ one nurse per shift

PharmacistCostPerShift.definition: Cost to employ one pharmacist per shift

objective.description: "Minimize the total number of healthcare workers scheduled (nurses plus pharmacists)"

constraints.description: Total labor hours provided by nurses and pharmacists must be at least 200 hours
Total cost of employing nurses and pharmacists must not exceed $9000
The number of nurses scheduled must be a non-negative integer
The number of pharmacists scheduled must be a non-negative integer
